description: Change points of a series by PELT: the exact minimum of the segment costs plus a penalty per change point. Arguments: series DOUBLE[], cost ('l2', 'normal', 'poisson', 'l1'), penalty (a number or 'bic', 'mbic', 'aic'), min_size.
comment: Returns the 1-based segment ends, the last one equal to the series length. NULL for an optional argument means its default: cost 'l2', penalty BIC, min_size 1. The example returns [3, 6].

description: Change points by binary segmentation: greedy, O(n log n). Arguments: series, cost, n_bkps (stop after that many splits) or penalty (stop when a split gains no more), min_size.
comment: Pass n_bkps or penalty, not both; with neither, the penalty is BIC. Use it for long series with few changes, where PELT gets slow. The example returns [3, 6, 9].

description: The optimal split of a series into exactly n_bkps + 1 segments (dynamic programming). Arguments: series, n_bkps, cost, min_size.
comment: O(n_bkps * n^2): meant for series up to about 1e4 points. The example returns [3, 6, 9].

description: Every distinct PELT segmentation for penalties in [pen_min, pen_max] (CROPS). Arguments: series, cost, pen_min, pen_max, min_size.
comment: Returns STRUCT(penalty, n_bkps, bkps)[] ordered by penalty; penalty is the smallest one at which PELT returns that segmentation. Useful to choose a penalty. The example returns two segmentations: [3, 6, 9] from penalty 0 and [9] from penalty 81.

description: Start, end (1-based, inclusive), mean, sample variance and length of every segment of a series, given its segment ends.
comment: bkps must be strictly increasing and end at the series length, as the other cpt functions return them. var is NULL for a one-element segment.
